hints: Focus on where chlorine and bromine sit in Group 17, chlorine is above bromine, so think about how atomic size changes down the group.
Remember that a smaller atom like chlorine forms a shorter, stronger bond to hydrogen and holds its own outer electron more tightly.
Now look for the property that gets bigger with more electrons and a larger electron cloud, as this will be weaker for the smaller chlorine molecule.
walkthrough:
**Place Chlorine and Bromine in Group 17**

Chlorine is above bromine in Group 17. This means a chlorine atom is smaller, with fewer shells and less shielding than a bromine atom.

Trend rule:
$$\text{atomic radius: Cl} < \text{Br}$$

**Check Properties That Are Larger For Chlorine**

A smaller atom gives a shorter, stronger $\text{H-X}$ bond, so $\text{H-Cl}$ is stronger than $\text{H-Br}$. It also holds outer electrons closer, so first ionisation energy is higher for chlorine.

$$\text{bond strength: H-Cl} > \text{H-Br}$$
$$\text{1st IE: Cl} > \text{Br}$$

**Check Silver Halide Solubility**

Silver chloride dissolves in dilute $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$, but silver bromide needs concentrated $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$. So solubility in $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$ is greater for the chloride.

$$\text{solubility: AgCl} > \text{AgBr}$$

**Identify The Property Smaller For Chlorine**

Van der Waals forces between $\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{Br}_2$ molecules are London dispersion forces. They increase with more electrons and a larger, more polarisable cloud.

$$\text{electrons: Br}_2 \text{(70)} > \text{Cl}_2 \text{(34)}$$
So dispersion forces are weaker for $\text{Cl}_2$ than for $\text{Br}_2$. This is the only property that is smaller for chlorine.

options.A: Incorrect. The H-Cl bond is stronger than the H-Br bond because Cl is smaller, giving better orbital overlap and a shorter bond. So bond strength is larger, not smaller, for chlorine.
options.B: Incorrect. First ionisation energy decreases down the group due to increased distance and shielding. Chlorine holds its 3p electron more tightly than bromine holds its 4p electron, so IE is larger for chlorine.
options.C: Incorrect. AgCl is more soluble in NH3(aq) than AgBr. AgCl dissolves in dilute NH3(aq) while AgBr only dissolves in concentrated NH3(aq), so solubility is larger for the chlorine compound.
options.D: Correct. Van der Waals (London dispersion) forces between X2 molecules increase down the group with more electrons and greater polarisability. Br2 has many more electrons than Cl2, so its dispersion forces are stronger, meaning they are smaller for chlorine.
